title: Ayodhya's 10th Deepotsav Is Tonight: 30 Lakh Diyas Planned Across 56 Ghats
excerpt: Ayodhya marks the 10th Deepotsav on Saturday, November 7, 2026, on the eve of Diwali, with organisers aiming to light more than 30 lakh earthen lamps across 56 ghats along the Saryu and Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan joining the celebrations.
body:
• Deepotsav 2026, the 10th edition of Ayodhya's festival of lights, is held today, Saturday, November 7, 2026, on the eve of Diwali, which falls on Sunday, November 8.
  • Organisers aim to light more than 30 lakh earthen diyas across 56 ghats along the Saryu river, centred on Ram Ki Paidi; the final lit count will only be known after the event.
  • Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan is attending, with prayers at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple and a symbolic coronation ceremony on the programme, according to an official statement.
  • A 2,100-drone show is planned for tonight, November 7, with a repeat performance scheduled for November 9, the Uttar Pradesh Tourism Department said.

Ayodhya is preparing to illuminate itself with 30 lakh lamps on Saturday as Deepotsav-2026, the city's annual festival of lights, reaches its 10th edition, PTI reported. From the ghats to major roads and religious sites, preparations involving lighting, decoration and cultural programmes have given the city a festive appearance ahead of the evening lighting, according to India Today.

Plan Your Visit

  • Date: Saturday, November 7, 2026 (main celebration; Deepotsav events run November 6-8)
  • Venue: Ram Ki Paidi and 56 ghats along the Saryu river, Ayodhya, Uttar Pradesh
  • Highlights: Mass diya lighting at dusk; 2,100-drone show on November 7, repeated November 9
  • Admission: Not stated in the announcements — check the Uttar Pradesh Tourism Department's Deepotsav release before travelling.
  • Official page: Uttar Pradesh Tourism Deepotsav 2026 release

The scale of tonight's lighting

Organisers are aiming to illuminate more than 30 to 33 lakh earthen diyas across 56 ghats, with the primary centre at Ram Ki Paidi and along the banks of the Saryu river, according to an official statement reported by Nation Press. The figures are a plan, not a result: the number of lamps actually lit can only be counted after the event. Dr Rammanohar Lohia Avadh University, which is coordinating the arrangements, procured 33 lakh diyas against the target of lighting 30 lakh, to account for breakage during transportation and placement, the Uttar Pradesh government said in a statement carried by PTI. This year, diyas will be arranged across 56 ghats, including the expanded Ram Ki Paidi, Chaudhary Charan Singh Ghat and Bhajan Sandhya Sthal.

The Vice-President attends

Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan will travel to Ayodhya on Saturday to participate in Deepotsav 2026, according to an official statement. He will offer prayers at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple, participate in the symbolic coronation ceremony of Lord Ram and felicitate saints, according to the Vice-President's Secretariat as reported by IANS. The visit marks the 10th anniversary of the festival, held annually on the eve of Diwali under Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's government. The state government said the festival's global recognition is setting an example of taking Uttar Pradesh's cultural heritage to new heights, PTI reported.

What Deepotsav marks

Deepotsav celebrates the return of Lord Ram to Ayodhya after his victory over Ravana and the completion of his fourteen years of exile, and is organised a day before Diwali, on Choti Diwali, according to the Uttar Pradesh Tourism Department. Led by the Department of Tourism, this year's celebrations combine traditional rituals with contemporary visual experiences, including the drone displays and illuminated riverfronts. Tourism and Culture Minister Jaiveer Singh said Deepotsav 2026 will offer visitors from India and across the world an opportunity to experience Ayodhya's spiritual heritage, traditions and hospitality.

The festival began in 2017 and has expanded considerably over the past decade. For visitors, the main viewing is along the Saryu riverfront at Ram Ki Paidi; the drone show is scheduled for tonight with a repeat on November 9 for those who miss the first performance.
